newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian conglomerates lower in weak share trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian conglomerates lower in weak share trade.

text.p: Nigerian conglomerates fell further on Wednesday on the Nigerian stock exchange, weighed down by continuous selling, traders said.
Due to technical problems the all-share index was not updated.
Most of the companies ended lower, led by PZ Industries, down five kobo at 28.45 naira.
Franco-Nigerian groups CFAO and SCOA ended two kobo lower each at 3.37 naira and 1.85 naira, respectively.
UAC lost 10 kobo to 16.50 naira while Lever Brothers closed unchanged.
Dealers said investors were selling to raise cash to cope with a lingering fuel scarcity which has further worsened the country's economy.
Banking shares were also weaker except for UBA which appreciated by 25 kobo to 11.15 naira because investors considered it cheap.
Wema Bank also rose five kobo to 3.35 naira because of its attractive price.
But First Bank and Union Bank who, together with UBA are the nation's biggest three financial institutions, slumped.
First Bank closed at 13.30 naira, down 10 kobo and Union Bank ended 15 kobo lower at 11.05 naira.

Traders who were not impressed with healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham's recent full-year result shaved off two kobo from its price. It ended at 5.87 naira despite the company's explanation that the result of its merger with Sterling Products would soon start to show.
Positive sentiments continued to move Nestle. It rose 30 kobo to 50.00 naira on Wednesday.
Petroleum marketers had a respite as only Agip suffered a drop, closing 10 kobo down at 18.30 naira.
